sources.title: UNESCO: Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork
sources.note: 1309 transfer, Gothic brick construction, crusades and forced conversion, conservation and wartime restoration.

sources.title: Malbork Castle Museum: Gdanisko
sources.note: Medieval latrine tower above running water, defensive refuge, early movable wooden passage and later masonry corridor.

sources.title: Malbork Castle Museum: Medieval heating system
sources.note: Fieldstone heat storage, floor outlets and covers, fuel economy; most surviving stoves rebuilt in nineteenth century.

sources.title: Malbork Castle Museum: Discovered hypocaust-type furnace
sources.note: Excavated furnace at new research centre; among earliest at castle, report supplies no precise date. Previously known example under Great Refectory dated 1330s.

sources.title: Malbork Castle Museum: Infirmary
sources.note: Care for old/infirm knights, separate dining room/chapel/bath, sickroom with adjoining toilet; later Polish use and twentieth-century restorations.

sources.title: Malbork Castle Museum: Kitchen and cook’s chamber
sources.note: Kitchen north of Great Refectory, large hearth and hood, cook’s room and store; early twentieth-century painted drapery.

sources.title: Malbork Castle Museum: High Castle interiors
sources.note: Convent room music gallery, treasury suite, surviving mill equipment; modern door inscription copied from Margat is not used as a medieval Malbork witness.

sources.title: Bavarian State Library: Petrus de Dusburg, Chronicon Prussiae
sources.note: 1679 printed edition, author fourteenth-century Peter of Dusburg, subject chronology 1205-1325, shelfmark 4 Bor.14. Sample uses actual short printed title and identifies later edition.

sources.title: National History Museum of Latvia: Courland, Semigallia and Lithuania exhibition
sources.note: Livonia multiple centres, Order’s Livonian branch;1561 submission and Kettler’s duchy.

sources.title: Polish Integrated Education Platform: European Power, lesson plan
sources.note: 1519-1521 war; Albert adopted Lutheranism and transformed Prussian monastic state into secular duchy;1525 homage.

sources.title: Teutonic Order: Our roots
sources.note: Institutional history of hospital origins near Acre 1190 and continuing religious/social work. Promotional claims about first field hospital are not adopted.

proposedOverrides.name: Teutonic Order in Prussia and Livonia

batchIdentityNotes.note: Decoded 1279,1400 and 1500 features span about 18.28-27.93 E and 53.10-59.49 N, combining Prussia and Livonia. This requires separate 1525 Prussian and 1561 Livonian endings. Coarse map boundaries do not resolve other Livonian authorities; no polygon certified or changed. Most daily-life evidence concerns Malbork’s elite religious household, not all Baltic families.
